sb.title: Sandbox
sb.desc: Limits what this program can reach: files, network and resources.
sb.process.unconfirmed: Not reported. The computer does not say whether the running program is the sandboxed one: a policy applies when the program starts.
sb.configured.inactive: Saved, but it restricts nothing, so nothing is used
sb.effective.notValid: Nothing: the saved policy no longer passes the computer's checks (see below)
sb.live.draining: Rules of an earlier run stay until that run stops
sb.unconfined: An earlier copy of this program may still be running UNCONFINED, without its sandbox. Until it stops, its firewall rules and ports stay reserved.
sb.missing: This computer lacks {{parts}}, which this policy needs. The program will not start until that is installed or the policy changes.
sb.part.landlock: a kernel with Landlock version 4 or newer
sb.part.tmpfs_size: a sandbox runtime that can size the temporary folder
sb.hostFirewall: This computer's inbound firewall is degraded, so inbound limits may not hold.
sb.disabled: This program is turned off. The policy applies when it is turned on; saving may clean up a loaded copy.
sb.system: System programs keep the sandbox they ship with. You can view it here but not change it.
sb.systemOff: This system program is off. Its policy applies when it is on; you can view it but not change it.
sb.readFailed: Could not read this program's sandbox.
sb.staleData: Couldn't refresh: this is the last answer the computer gave.
sb.lifeBusy: A start, stop or restart of this program is still waiting. Sandbox changes wait until it is confirmed.
sb.malformed: The computer's answer about this sandbox could not be read.
sb.tech.noTable: The inbound table is not present.
sb.w.ports: Ports named: {{ports}} (listening is not limited in this network mode)
sb.w.inbound: New inbound IPv4 TCP connections from outside to its listening ports only from {{list}}; replies to its own connections pass
sb.w.rate: Each address: at most {{rate}} new inbound IPv4 TCP connections to its listening ports (a short burst passes)
sb.w.noLocal: The computer's own and the platform's connections are filtered too
sb.w.platform: The computer's own and the platform's connections are not filtered
sb.w.otherPorts: Other ports it listens on are not filtered (listening is not limited in this network mode)
sb.ed.title: Sandbox for {{name}}
sb.ed.sub: Limits its files, network and resources from its next start.
sb.ed.factsFailed: Could not read the program, so only the policy's own rules are checked here. The computer checks the rest when you save.
sb.ed.preset.noNetwork.d: The program cannot connect anywhere or listen on any port.
sb.ed.preset.noNetwork.hasPorts: This program listens on a port, so it needs some network.
sb.ed.preset.noOutgoingTcp.d: It can still answer on its own ports. UDP is not covered.
sb.ed.preset.readOnly.d: Add folders it may write to below.
sb.ed.preset.limits.d: Memory 512 MB, 256 processes and its own temporary folder.
sb.actionsWait: Waiting until the sandbox change is confirmed or you stop tracking it.
sb.ed.used: Used: the fields below now hold it. Save sends it.
sb.ed.writable: Folders it may still write to
sb.ed.writable.d: One full path per line. Needs read-only files.
sb.ed.hidden.d: One full path per line. The program sees these as empty.
sb.ed.mode.restricted.d: Listens only on its ports; outgoing TCP only to the ports below.
sb.ed.mode.none.d: No network at all. Only for programs without ports.
sb.ed.connectPorts.off: Only applies when Connections is Limited.
sb.ed.ingressFrom.d: IPv4 ranges like 203.0.113.0/24, separated by spaces. A range here can shut web visitors out. Empty means anyone.
sb.ed.allowPlatform: Let the computer's own connections through unfiltered
sb.ed.allowPlatform.d: The computer and its gateway skip these checks.
sb.ed.programProblems: The computer will refuse a sandbox for this program until these are fixed in its settings:
sb.ed.restart: Saving may restart the program if it is running and the change affects how it starts.
sb.ed.restartOff: The program is turned off: the policy applies when it is turned on. Saving may clean up a loaded copy.
sb.ed.noopRemove: These settings restrict nothing. To run it without limits, remove the sandbox below.
sb.ed.removeRow.d: Drops every limit above, from its next start.
sb.ed.unsupported: Editing is off for this sandbox. It has settings this page can't edit ({{fields}}), and saving would drop them. Remove sandbox still removes the whole policy.
sb.ed.hostFirewall: This computer's inbound firewall is degraded: inbound limits may not hold even once saved.
sb.ed.removeBody: The program runs without these limits from its next start. If it is running, it may restart now.
sb.out.saved: Saved. What the computer reports now is shown in the panel.
sb.out.savedRunning: Saved. {{name}} was running, so the new limits apply from its next restart.
sb.restartAskBody: {{name}} stops for a moment, then starts again with the saved limits. Whatever it is doing now is interrupted.
sb.out.notApplied: The policy was saved, but the computer reported it could not apply it. The computer said: {{text}}
sb.out.notAppliedPlain: The policy was saved, but the computer reports it is not applied.
sb.out.removeNotApplied: The policy was removed from the program, but the computer reported it could not apply that. The computer said: {{text}}
sb.out.removeNotAppliedPlain: The policy was removed from the program, but the computer reports that is not applied.
sb.ed.changed: This sandbox changed after you opened it. Saved now: {{lines}}. Press Save again to replace it with yours.
sb.ed.readFailed: Couldn't read the saved policy before saving, so nothing was sent. Try again.
sb.out.refusedPlain: Not saved. The computer refused the change.
sb.out.tooLarge: Not saved: the policy is too large for the computer.
sb.out.dismissBody: It may still have gone through. After this, Save sends a new change; check the saved policy first.
sb.out.unknown: The computer's answer did not say whether the policy was saved. Check again reads the saved policy; it never sends again.
sb.out.stillUnknown: The saved policy is not the one you sent, so it is still not known whether yours went through. Another change may have replaced it.
sb.out.readFailed: Could not read the saved policy. Try Check again in a moment.
sb.out.notSent: Not sent: another change to this program's sandbox is still waiting.
sb.out.stale: Not sent: the account or computer changed. Open the editor again.
sb.out.elsewhere: A sandbox change for this program is waiting in another tab or page. Check it there.
sb.out.reapplied: Applied again. What the computer reports now is shown in the panel.
sb.out.reapplyReadFailed: Not sent: the saved policy could not be read first. Press Apply saved policy again in a moment.
sb.out.reapplyChanged: Not sent: the computer now stores another policy than the one that failed. It is shown under Saved policy; open the editor to change it.
sb.out.storedUnconfirmed: Your policy is the stored one, but the computer does not report whether applying it again worked. Check the program, then close this note.
sb.err.root: It runs as root. A sandbox needs another user.
sb.err.terminal: It runs in a terminal. A sandbox needs a program without one.
sb.err.runUser: Its folder is under /run/user, which a sandbox cannot use.
sb.err.env.name: Its setting {{name}} is not a valid variable name.
sb.err.env.loader: Its setting {{name}} could change how programs load, which a sandbox refuses.
sb.err.env.reserved: Its setting {{name}} uses a name the sandbox reserves.
sb.err.env.value: Its setting {{name}} holds a character a sandbox refuses (% ' " \ or a control character).
sb.err.display: Its display setting holds a character a sandbox refuses.
sb.err.privateTmpDirectory: Its folder is inside a temporary folder, which its own temporary folder would hide.
sb.err.writableNeedsRo: Turn on read-only files to list folders it may write to.
sb.err.pathAbsolute: {{path}} must be a full path starting with /.
sb.err.protected: {{path}} is inside {{root}}, which the computer protects.
sb.err.privateTmpWritable: {{path}} is inside a temporary folder, which its own temporary folder replaces.
sb.err.hiddenDirectory: {{path}} would hide the program's own folder.
sb.err.hiddenWritable: {{path}} overlaps {{other}}, a folder it may write to.
sb.err.port: {{item}} is not a port or port range (1 to 65535).
sb.err.cidr: {{item}} is not an IPv4 range like 203.0.113.0/24.
sb.err.rate: Use a number from 1 to 100000 then /s or /m, like 50/s.
sb.err.connectNeedsRestricted: Outgoing ports only apply when connections are Limited.
sb.err.noneHasPorts: This program listens on a port, so it cannot have no network.
sb.err.noneBind: With no network, it cannot listen on ports.
sb.err.noneInbound: With no network, there is no inbound traffic to limit.
sb.err.restrictedNeedsPorts: Limited connections need at least one port it listens on.
sb.err.bindCovers: The list must include every port the program uses.
sb.err.inboundNeedsPorts: Inbound limits need at least one port it listens on.
sb.err.tmpNeedsPrivate: Turn on its own temporary folder to set a size.
np.title: New program
np.sub: Add program keeps it. Run now starts it once.
np.mode.keep.d: Saved on this computer. Start it when you like, or with the computer.
np.mode.once.d: Starts now and isn't kept. After it ends, its result stays readable for 10 minutes.
np.name: Name
np.name.d: Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores. Each program on this computer has its own name.
np.name.dOnce: Optional. Leave it empty and one is made up.
np.command.d: The whole command line, like node server.js. For your own code; system services are managed elsewhere.
np.user.d: The Linux account it runs under.
np.ports.range: A range: one copy per port
np.port.d: Write it in the command too. A start counts as done once this port answers.
np.range.d: Each port gets its own copy of the program, up to 4096.
np.portParam.d: Written before each port number. Leave it empty for --port.
np.boot.d: It may also start when added.
np.err.nameChars: Start with a letter or digit, then use letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores.
np.err.nameTaken: This computer already has a program with this name.
np.err.commandLine: Keep the command on one line.
np.err.userChars: Use an account name, like user.
np.err.rangeOrder: The last port can't come before the first.
np.err.rangeSize: A range holds 4096 ports at most.
np.err.paramChars: Start with - or --, then a letter, like --port or -p.
np.out.tooLarge: That's more than the computer takes in one request.
np.out.read: Couldn't read this computer's programs, so nothing was sent. Try again.
np.out.taken: This computer already has a program named {{name}}. Nothing was sent.
np.out.takenOnce: A temporary program named {{name}} is already here. Pick another name; nothing was sent.
np.out.held: An earlier send of {{name}} still has no answer, so nothing more was sent.
np.out.storage: This browser can't keep track of the send, so nothing was sent.
np.out.full: Too many sends are waiting for an answer. Check or stop tracking them first; nothing was sent.
np.out.stale: The account or computer changed before it left. Nothing was sent.
np.held.keep: We can't tell yet whether {{name}} was added.
np.held.once: We can't tell yet whether {{name}} started.
np.held.body: It may have gone through. Check reads the list again and never sends it twice.
np.check.notYet: Not in the list yet. The computer may still be working on it.
np.check.readFailed: Couldn't read the list. Try again.
np.check.inFlight: Still waiting for the computer's answer.
np.dismissBody: {{name}} may still be on the computer. Look at the list before you add it again.
np.problem.keep: {{name}} was added, but its settings aren't applied yet, so it isn't running.
np.problem.once: {{name}} was created, but it didn't start.
np.found.keep: A program named {{name}} is on this computer now. It may be from this send or from somewhere else.
np.found.onceUnknown: {{name}} is listed; we can't tell yet whether it started.
np.check.listed: A temporary program named {{name}} is listed, but it may be from somewhere else, so this send stays tracked. Stop tracking it once you're sure.
np.directory.d: An absolute path on the computer that already exists. Empty: the account's home folder.
np.description.d: A note for you. The program never sees it.
np.env.d: Values are kept in the program's settings and can be read there and in its logs.
np.startSecs.d: How long it must keep running before the start counts as done. Empty or 0 means 1 second. If it crashes in that time, the start failed. If it ends normally in that time, the restart setting above decides.
np.logs: Keep its output in log files
np.logs.d: Off: nothing it prints is kept.
np.logSize.d: A full log starts a new one. 0: never. Empty: 5 MB.
np.sb: Limit what this program can do
np.sb.d: The same choices as the program's Sandbox panel. Leave it as it is for no sandbox.
np.sb.on: This program will start inside a sandbox.
np.sb.programProblems: The computer will refuse this sandbox until these are fixed above:
np.err.pathChars: Use letters, digits, spaces, /, _, . and - only.
np.err.envName: {{name}}: start with a letter or _, then letters, digits or _ (128 at most).
np.err.envNameEmpty: Row {{n}}: give the variable a name.
np.err.envLine: {{name}}: keep the value on one line.
np.err.envComment: {{name}}: the value has a space before ; or #, which would cut it short.
np.err.envQuotes: {{name}}: the value has both " and ', which the computer can't store as written.
np.err.envQuoteEnd: {{name}}: the value starts or ends with a quote, which would be dropped.
np.err.envExpansion: {{name}}: the value has a %(…) the computer can't fill in. Write %% for a plain %.
np.err.sbEnv.loader: {{name}} could change how programs load, which a sandbox refuses.
np.err.sbEnv.reserved: {{name}} uses a name the sandbox reserves.
np.err.sbEnv.value: {{name}}: in a sandbox, a value can't hold % ' " \ or a control character.
np.out.withheld: Its answer isn't shown because it held one of your environment values.
np.startSecs.q: What if it has a port?
np.startSecs.why: With a port, a start counts as done once that port answers.
np.mode.why: Keep it for something you will start again, such as a server. Run once for a single job.
np.mode.more: More about Keep it and Run once
sb.editOff: The sandbox can't be changed until its status is read and any earlier change is confirmed.
